acme_rep: Hey team — rerank endpoint is behaving weirdly for us. We followed the console cURL example in the docs but get a mix of 400s and scores > 1. Repro steps below and exact request/response we used.

acme_rep: cURL we ran from macOS terminal (copied from docs):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"best redwood deployment practices","documents":"doc1\ndoc2\ndoc3"}'
```

acme_rep: Response: HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"invalid_payload","message":"expected array for 'documents' got string"}

maya: thanks — can you paste the exact JSON you put in? console snippets sometimes get mangled when folks copy from the web UI.

acme_rep: pasted above. also tried sending file with --data-binary @payload.json and then got 200 but scores are weird: some docs have score 3.14, some -2.1. We expected normalized [0,1].

eli: quick triage notes: two separate issues seem plausible here — (1) docs/curl example incorrectly shows "documents" as a newline string instead of an array/object shape we expect, and (2) scoring semantics changed in a recent deploy (raw logits returned unless you request normalization).

jon: confirming — current API expects payload shape: {"query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"..."}, ...]} not a single "documents" newline string. Our old docs had an inline helper that turned arrays into newline-delimited strings for the web console and that got copied into the cURL example. That explains the 400.

jon: for the unexpected score values: the endpoint returns raw model scores by default (pre-normalization). There is an optional query param "normalize=true" (or body field "normalize_scores": true) to get [0,1] probabilities. Docs were inconsistent across pages — some examples show normalize=true, others don't.

acme_rep: ah ok that matches. why did --data-binary produce 200 then? we tried two ways: first the inline -d ... string (400), then wrote payload.json with the documents array and used --data-binary @payload.json and got 200 but the numbers were raw.

eli: exactly — when you fixed payload shape you cleared the 400. The raw scores are a separate thing.

maya: can you share the payload.json that produced 200? also which version of CLI / curl? some shells (zsh with certain aliases) can re-interpret newlines unless you use proper quoting.

acme_rep: payload.json we used: {"query":"best redwood deployment practices","candidates":[{"id":"a","text":"Use dedicated capacity."},{"id":"b","text":"Cache KV prefixes."},{"id":"c","text":"Quantize models."}]}

acme_rep: curl used: curl 7.85.0 on mac. response body snippet: {"results":[{"id":"a","score":3.1842},{"id":"b","score":-2.103},{"id":"c","score":0.12}]}

eli: thanks. that looks right for raw logits. For normalization use: POST /v1/rerank?normalize=true or add "normalize_scores": true to the body. We'll confirm which API is canonical and update docs.

sara: tagging this for docs fixes. I found two pages: "Rerank API (Console)" and "Rerank REST examples" where examples diverge. One shows "documents": "a\nb\nc" (copied from the web console helper) and the other shows "candidates" correctly. I'm going to open a quick PR to unify examples and add a note about normalize_scores.

sara: may I also add a small troubleshooting tip about shell quoting and using --data-binary @payload.json to avoid newline mangling?

jon: yes please. add a snippet that uses jq to build candidates array too. Eg: 
```bash
jq -n --arg q "best x" --argjson c '[{"id":"1","text":"a"}]' '{query:$q, candidates:$c}' > payload.json
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/rerank?normalize=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @payload.json
```

eli: operational note: we also had a soft limit change last quarter — candidate_limit is 100 now (docs previously said 200). If you send >100 you'll get 422 with message: "candidate limit exceeded". That might be another pain point for some customers.

acme_rep: we did a large batch (150) in an earlier test and got a 422, so that explains it — thanks. Any ETA for docs fix?

sara: I'll do a small PR today to: 1) update cURL/console examples to canonical JSON shape, 2) note candidate_limit=100 and error message, 3) show normalize_scores example. Putting in review now.

maya: I'll follow up with the customer and share the corrected cURL + payload examples and mention the candidate limit and score normalization.

eli: internal follow-up for runtime: can we add a clearer error when someone sends newline string for documents? Current error is generic invalid_payload. If we detect the specific pattern (string with newlines) return 400 with message: "expected array/object for candidates; got newline-delimited string (see docs)" — that will save support time.

jon: +1 — filed ticket INF-4272 to add better validation message and link to docs.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-23: Rerank docs/curl inconsistency (linked to INF-4272).

acme_rep: great, thanks everyone. small ask — when you push doc fixes can you ping me here so I can validate the examples with our internal automation?

maya: will do. feel free to DM if you want hand-holding while running the corrected requests. :thumbsup:

jon: quick final — canonical corrected cURL example to include in docs: 
```bash
cat > payload.json <<'JSON'
{"query":"best redwood deployment practices","candidates":[{"id":"1","text":"Use dedicated capacity."},{"id":"2","text":"Cache KV prefixes."}]}
JSON

curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/rerank?normalize=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @payload.json | jq .
```

sara: PR filed: https://git.redwood-inference.com/docs/pull/987 (will update after review).

maya: closing loop once docs live. thanks all :eyes:
